gap: The great wall and most building facades read as one flat, tiled cardboard texture with no bevel, weathering, or scale cues, so it never registers as the city-swallowing colossal structure it is in the game.

shots.comparison: Reference wins: soft fog and cool light sell the wall's mass and depth, while ours is flat midday light on a cartoonish, obviously-tiled checkerboard wall texture.
Reference wins: warm painterly haze and color grading over dense rooftops vs. ours' clean but flat, atmosphere-less brown roof mass with no smoke or haze.
Reference wins: game shows a legible plaza and varied landmark buildings; ours is homogeneous repeated roof kits with no focal landmark to anchor the eye.
Reference wins: the game street has layered depth, foliage, and painterly light shafts; ours is a stiff, empty corridor with an unexplained floating pale object breaking the illusion.
Reference wins outright: ours is a broken shot with the camera clipped inside roof/wall geometry, unusable as a game-quality frame at all.
Reference wins: game alley has hanging signage with real material depth and foliage; ours has flat solid-color placeholder banner cards and blurry, tiled stone.
Reference wins: same wall-scale and atmosphere gap, ours stays a washed-out grey-brown haze with no golden-hour warmth despite a visible sun.
Reference wins: the game frame is a cinematic gold sunbeam through smoke; ours is a competently staged fountain plaza but lit flat and contrasty, with boxy characterless buildings.
Reference wins, though this is our best-dressed street with cart and barrels; the game's texture fidelity, lighting falloff, and depth still read a tier above.
Closest tonal match of the set, but reference still wins: the game's dusk sky has cloud detail and character-driven mood while ours is a flat, empty navy gradient over underlit buildings.
Reference wins: same placeholder-flag and flat-stone texture problem as town_canyon, though the alley massing and window rhythm are reasonably close.
